newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-PICABO STREET OUT FOR SEASON AFTER TRAINING INJURY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-PICABO STREET OUT FOR SEASON AFTER TRAINING INJURY.

text.p: Defending World Cup downhill champion Picabo Street of the United States suffered a season-ending knee injuring during a training-run crash on Wednesday.
Street fell on a steep face near the finish of the first practice run for Friday's World Cup downhill in Vail.

Dr Richard Steadman, U.S. Ski Team physician, diagnosed the injury as a complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament of her left knee. Street also incurred less serious damage to the cartilage and other ligaments of the same knee.
Steadman, who will perform surgery next week when the swelling subsides, said Street will be off skis for six months.
"I'm OK. I'm bummed, but I'm OK," said Street, who skidded 75 metres down the steep headwall before crashing into a safety net.

Street, 25, has been the dominant downhill racer over the past two seasons, winning nine races while claiming two overall downhill titles. She is also the reigning world champion and won the silver medal at the 1994 Olympics.
